name: Destination Thailand Visa (DTV)

requirement_groups.name: Workcation (remote work for a foreign-registered employer)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires employment by, or freelance contracts with, a company or clients registered outside Thailand -- working for Thai companies or Thai clients is not covered and remains subject to Non-B/work permit rules instead.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the employing or contracting entity is genuinely foreign-registered.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires proof of funds of at least THB 500,000 (roughly USD 14,000).
requirements.fix_path: Document at least THB 500,000 in available funds.

requirements.blocker_text: Covers participants in Muay Thai training, Thai culinary arts courses, medical treatment, professional seminars, or artistic/cultural festivals -- a genuinely distinct qualifying basis from remote employment, aimed at attracting participation in Thai cultural and soft-power activities specifically.
requirements.fix_path: Enrol in or secure participation confirmation for a qualifying Thai soft-power activity.

evidence_required.document: Employment/freelance contract with a foreign-registered entity, or confirmation of a qualifying soft-power activity

outcome.duration_length: 5 years multiple-entry, up to 180 days per entry, extendable once per entry for a further 180 days at an immigration office
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: must exit and re-enter Thailand every ~180 days to maintain status; DTV years do not count toward the LTR visa or Thai Permanent Residency

sources.title: Issa Compass -- Visa Options for Digital Nomads in Thailand, describing the DTV's THB 500,000 funds requirement and foreign-employer test
MBMG Group -- DTV vs. LTR: The Definitive Guide to Thailand's Long-Term Visas (2026 Update), describing the Workcation and Thai Soft Power & Activities categories

notes: STATUS: DRAFT. HONEST SOURCING GAP: no direct fetch of a Thai e-Visa or MFA government page was achieved for this route in this research pass. STRUCTURAL FINDING: the DTV's legal status for remote work occupies a genuine grey area, confirmed across multiple independent sources -- the visa authorises the stay but does not explicitly grant formal work permission the way th_smart_visa or th_non_b_work_permit do, since Thailand's Foreign Business Act and Alien Employment Act frameworks were not written with remote/foreign-employer work in mind. DTV time explicitly does NOT count toward LTR visa eligibility or Thai Permanent Residency, confirmed across multiple sources -- a real structural dead-end distinguishing this route from most other work_independent routes in this dataset (contrast with Poland's D-8-4 or Italy's self-employment visa, both of which do lead toward settlement); leads_to_pr and leads_to_citizenship are correctly false rather than merely unpopulated. The 180-day exit/re-entry cycle (rather than a single continuous 5-year stay) is a genuinely distinctive maintenance requirement among this dataset's long-stay routes -- DTV holders routinely use these mandatory exits as informal regional travel opportunities (Malaysia, Singapore, Vietnam commonly cited), a real, documented practical pattern worth surfacing. The two qualifying groups (Workcation and Thai Soft Power & Activities) are genuinely distinct in purpose -- one economic/remote-work-oriented, one cultural-participation-oriented -- correctly modeled as separate OR-logic groups rather than blended into one generic 'DTV' test.
